en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect conical shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Babuyan Channel.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is a critically endangered bird endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the South China Sea.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the largest lake in the southern Philippines and serves as a major source of hydroelectric power.
Mount Apo, located in Mindanao, is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected marine sanctuary in the Sulu Sea known for its pristine coral reefs and diverse marine life.
The southwest monsoon, locally called Habagat, brings heavy rainfall to the western parts of the Philippines between June and October.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest nickel reserves, primarily mined in the provinces of Surigao del Norte and Palawan.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is a complex volcano situated entirely within a large caldera lake called Taal Lake.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes adapted for nocturnal hunting.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are ancient agricultural structures carved into the mountainsides over 2,000 years ago by indigenous ancestors.
